title: How to harvest okra
seoTitle: How to Harvest Okra: When to Pick and How Often
description: Pick okra pods at 2 to 4 inches long, every day or two, before they turn tough. How to cut them, keep the plant producing and store the harvest.
summary: Pick okra pods when they're 2 to 4 inches long, and pick every day or two. Pods grow fast and turn tough and woody if you wait, and regular picking keeps the plant producing.

intro: Okra rewards the gardener who shows up. Once the plants start producing, there are new pods ready almost every day, and the difference between tender and tough is often just a day or two.
New to okra? Start with [how to grow okra](/okra/how-to-grow-okra), or get [free okra seeds](/okra/free-okra-seeds) from Olivia's garden.

items: First pods about 2 months after planting
Cut the stem, don't pull the pod
Refrigerate unwashed and use within a week

blocks.text: Okra plants [flower about 2 months after planting](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/), and each pod is ready to pick 3 to 4 days after its flower opens. Pick pods while they're 2 to 4 inches long. Clemson Extension notes that [2 to 3 inch pods are still tender](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), while bigger pods get tougher and more fibrous.
A pod that's ready snaps or slices easily and the tip bends a little. If the knife drags or the pod feels hard and woody, it waited too long.

Pick every day or two. Texas A&M AgriLife warns that if you don't pick [every 1 to 2 days, yields will decrease](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/). Pods left to mature signal the plant that its job is done, and it slows down.

Picked often and kept watered, okra can keep producing [for up to 12 weeks](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), and in a long, hot summer it often goes until frost.

items: Cut each pod with [pruners or a sharp knife](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), leaving a short piece of stem on the pod. Pulling can tear the branch.
Handle the pods gently. They bruise easily, and bruised spots turn dark.
Check the whole plant, including the undersides of leaves. Pods hide, and a missed one turns woody in a few days.

sections.title: Okra pods too big or woody

blocks.text: Pods that grew too long are tough and stringy, and cooking won't soften them. Cut them off anyway, so the plant puts its energy into new pods.
Overgrown pods aren't wasted. Toss them in the compost, or leave a few on the plant to dry and [save the seeds](/okra/saving-okra-seeds) for next year.

Don't wash okra until you're ready to cook it, since washing [speeds up decay](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/) in the refrigerator. Store the pods dry, and use them within a few days. Well-handled pods can last up to a week.

faq.question: How big should okra be when you pick it?
faq.answer: About 2 to 4 inches long. Smaller pods are the most tender. Past about 4 inches most pods turn tough and fibrous.

faq.question: Why is my okra tough and woody?
faq.answer: It stayed on the plant too long. Okra grows fast, so a pod can go from tender to woody in a day or two. Pick every day or two to keep up.

faq.question: How often should you harvest okra?
faq.answer: Every day or two once the plants start producing. Regular picking keeps the plant making new pods.

faq.question: Does okra keep producing after you pick it?
faq.answer: Yes. Picking encourages new pods, and well-watered plants keep producing for weeks, often until frost.
